conflict_synopsis.core_view: US hike-cycle and SOFR-path uptrend persist after the delivered 25bp hike; fading 99th-percentile US yields is premature.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Broadening global tightening after the Fed hike (BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6-3, energy shock constraining easing) while SOFR still prices only +35bp by December.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Front SOFR strip flattening back to overnight or a 2023-02-style financial-stress reversal.

paper_capital.rationale: Funded seats pay 5% ACT/365 on the full $100m whether flat or not, so HOLD has no cash yield and only the vig. A $10m short US 2Y starter OPEN is the risk unit that can harvest hike-cycle analog continuation (2022-03-23 +59bp 1m / +88bp 3m; 2022-09-16 +58bp / +40bp) without pretending the packet supplies executable marks. Expected rates PnL is positive versus being flat; the parent should execution-block rather than this seat inventing a broker price. $10m is intentionally smaller than the $100m allocation because delayed SOFR and null stops cap sizing, not because the trend is faded.

remit: persistent price, rates and macro trends; reject premature fades
stance_summary: Ride the delivered US hike and still-rising SOFR path: hot US temps, broadening global tightening, and hike-cycle analogs all say the yield uptrend persists; fading 99th-percentile US yields or a one-and-done SOFR strip is a premature mean-reversion without a reversal catalyst.

Statistical stretch is the discovery screen, not the reversal signal.

policy_path_check.rationale: Inspected SOFR then CORRA then AONIA before sovereigns. The cleanest continuation is the US path: a delivered hike, still-hot US gauges, and a front SOFR strip that has not priced a continuing cycle. CORRA only +29bp by Dec is a lagging, not leading, hike trend and CA core inflation near 2% plus labor temp 38 argue against making CA the pay-side. AONIA is the steepest near-term hike path (+51bp to Mar 2027) but AU inflation temp 82 is paired with a documented housing downturn (the classic premature fade); AU 2Y 4.999 already sits above the 4.86 AONIA terminal, so paying AU sovereigns is paying through the cash path. NZ is dropped because B2 yields are blocked.

context_build.price_decomposition: FACT: overnight SOFR 3.85 is the post-hike cash anchor; the Sep contract at 3.75 is the monthly-average lag, not a cut. The Oct–Dec strip (3.91 / 4.045 / 4.1975) is the marginal policy-path component. US 2Y 4.76 minus SOFR = 91bp and minus Dec SOFR = 56bp, so sovereign 2Y already sits above the front path (term premium / extra hike odds). 2s10s at 25bp (0.2nd 1y percentile) shows the recent backup was led by the front end, not a bear-steepening. INFERENCE: continuation lives first in a higher SOFR strip (more hikes still coming) and then in 2Y remaining bid for higher yields; fading 2Y because it is above the current terminal confuses a still-rising path with a completed one. UNKNOWN: live AU OIS (2022 vintage only) and NZ sovereigns, so this decomposition is US-path first, then CA/AU cross-checks, not a four-country strip RV.

expression_comparison.rationale: The persistent object is the US policy path and the US 2Y uptrend, not FX. SOFR still prices only +6bp by Oct and +34.75bp by Dec after a delivered hike into hot US temperatures; that is the continuation discrepancy. USDCAD is a consistent but inferior expression: CAD has an energy terms-of-trade cushion (xa:energy-retained) and BoC energy pass-through that can scramble the FX transmission, while rates own the SOFR/2Y mechanism directly. Rates and spot both lack executable broker marks, so FX has no cleanliness advantage. Rates are preferred.

trade.mispricing: The mispricing is not ‘2Y is cheap’ — it is already above Dec SOFR and slightly above the Aug-2028 SOFR terminal. The mispricing is the market’s implicit terminal/fade assumption: that a delivered 25bp hike and 99th-percentile yields cap the cycle, so Oct SOFR at +6bp and Dec at +34.75bp are enough. That assumption is the premature fade. Continuation means the front path and 2Y keep repricing higher as global tightening and hot US temps persist.
